title: Alteration neighbourhoods regular over a J-2 quotient of a G-ring
statement: Let $B$ be a commutative Noetherian integral domain and a G-ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-g-ring], let $J\subseteq B$ be an ideal, and let $\mathfrak q\subset B$ be a prime ideal. Assume $B/J$ is J-2, meaning that the regular locus of every finite type $B/J$-algebra is open [def-exc-excellent-ring]. There exist $b\in B\setminus\mathfrak q$, a finite family of integral Noetherian schemes $X_i$ and dominant generically finite finite-type morphisms $\varphi_i:X_i\to Y=\operatorname{Spec}B[1/b]$ [def-pc-integral-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-ring-localization-away, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], with the following properties. For every $x\in\varphi_i^{-1}V(JB[1/b])$, the ambient local ring $\mathcal O_{X_i,x}$ is regular local [def-weil-regular-scheme]. There are an integral Noetherian scheme $V$, a proper surjective generically finite morphism $p:V\to Y$ [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism], a finite open cover $V=\bigcup_iV_i$, and $Y$-morphisms $V_i\to X_i$. Here $V(JB[1/b])$ denotes the set of primes containing the indicated ideal. Dominant means dense image; generically finite means that the induced extension of function fields is finite, with function field the local ring at the generic point. No universal catenarity of $B$ or excellence of $B_{\mathfrak q}$ is assumed.

source.place: Kurano–Shimomoto, Ideal-adic completion of quasi-excellent rings (after Gabber), Lemma 4.4, printed pp.5–6, and Definition 3.2, printed p.3. Specialization: the global G-ring B has G-ring localization B_q. Read online; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Put $A=B_{\mathfrak q}$. It is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian]. For a prime $Q\subset A$, [lem-weil-pbc-primes-of-localization] gives its contraction $\mathfrak r\subseteq\mathfrak q$, and [lem-weil-pbc-localize-localization-at-prime] identifies $A_Q$ with $B_{\mathfrak r}$ by the fraction map. This identifies their maximal ideals, their quotients by every power, and hence their inverse-limit completions and canonical completion maps. Each such map is regular by the G-ring hypothesis on $B$, so $A$ is a G-ring by [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]. The fraction construction also makes $A$ a nonzero local domain, with unique maximal ideal $\mathfrak qA$: a fraction with numerator outside $\mathfrak q$ is a unit, and a numerator in $\mathfrak q$ cannot be a unit. In particular $A$ is semilocal. Apply [lem-per-semilocal-g-ring-j2] to conclude that $A$ is quasi-excellent. Universal catenarity is not claimed.

source.place: Lemma 4.4, first sentence, printed p.5; Section 2, semilocal G-rings are quasi-excellent, printed p.2; Stacks 07GH and 00E3

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-qe-weak-uniformization-cover] to the nonempty integral Noetherian scheme $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$, whose one affine chart has quasi-excellent coordinate ring by Step 1. Obtain finitely many nonempty integral regular Noetherian schemes $T_i$, dominant generically finite finite-type maps $T_i\to S$, an integral Noetherian scheme $P$, a proper surjective generically finite map $P\to S$, a finite indexed open cover $P=\bigcup_iP_i$ and $S$-maps $P_i\to T_i$. This uses the ordinary alteration assertion, with no degree restriction.

source.place: Lemma 4.4, first proof paragraph, invoking Theorem 3.3 and Definition 3.2, printed pp.3,5

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-local-alteration-diagram-spreading] to the entire diagram of Step 2. It supplies $a\in B\setminus\mathfrak q$, integral Noetherian models $T_{a,i},P_a$ over $Y_a=\operatorname{Spec}B[1/a]$, dominant generically finite finite-type maps $f_i:T_{a,i}\to Y_a$, a proper surjective generically finite witness $P_a\to Y_a$, its finite indexed open cover and the maps into $T_{a,i}$. Its base change to $S$ is isomorphic to the specified diagram. Its permanence clause will retain all these properties after any further principal shrinking that contains $\mathfrak q$.

source.place: Lemma 4.4, first proof paragraph, spreading from B_q to B[1/tilde b], printed p.5; general limit input Stacks 081F

proof.text: Let $t\in T_{a,i}$ have image in $\operatorname{Spec}B$ a prime $\mathfrak r\subseteq\mathfrak q$. On an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}C$ containing $t$, write $\mathfrak p$ for its prime. Base change to $B_{\mathfrak q}$ inverts the images of $B\setminus\mathfrak q$ in $C$, all outside $\mathfrak p$. In the stalk $C_{\mathfrak p}$ these elements are already units; localizing first at them and then at the prime over $\mathfrak p$ gives the same fractions $c/u$, $u\notin\mathfrak p$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization], this is exactly the ambient stalk $\mathcal O_{T_{a,i},t}$ and the stalk of the corresponding point of $T_i$. The latter is regular by Step 2, so $\mathcal O_{T_{a,i},t}$ is regular. This establishes regularity over every generalization of $\mathfrak q$, rather than just its fibre.

source.place: Lemma 4.4, equation (4.3), printed p.5; affine localization calculation expanded, Stacks 01HV

proof.text: The composite $T_{a,i}\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ is finite type. Indeed $B[1/a]=B[u]/(au-1)$ is generated by $u$ over $B$, and finite type is preserved by composition by [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change]. Apply [lem-per-j2-closed-fibre-regular-locus] with $A=B$, $I=J$: its hypothesis is exactly the assumed J-2 property of $B/J$, without any G-ring requirement on that quotient. Thus $W_i=f_i^{-1}V(JB[1/a])\setminus\operatorname{Reg}(T_{a,i})$ is closed in $T_{a,i}$. Since that scheme is Noetherian, this closed subset is constructible by the Noetherian clause of [def-weil-constructible-subset]. The local rings here are those of the ambient $T_{a,i}$, not those of its closed fibre.

source.place: Lemma 4.4, definition of W and application of Lemma 4.2, printed p.5; Stacks 01T3 and 005L

proof.text: The base ring $B[1/a]$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian]. On an affine cover for the finite-type map $f_i$, each finite-type algebra over this base is finitely presented by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-noetherian-finite-presentation]. Consequently $f_i$ is locally of finite presentation; it is quasi-compact because it is finite type. The affine scheme $Y_a$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-chevalley-constructible-image] applies to the constructible $W_i$ of Step 5 and shows that $E_i=f_i(W_i)$ is constructible in $Y_a$.

source.place: Lemma 4.4, Chevalley paragraph, printed p.5; Stacks 00FN, 00FP, 054J

proof.text: The affine qcqs scheme $Y_a$ is spectral by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-scheme-spectral]. Suppose its point $\mathfrak qB[1/a]$ belonged to $\overline{E_i}$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-spectral-proconstructible-closure-specialization] to the one-member family consisting of $E_i$. It gives $e\in E_i$ generalizing this point. Under the basic-open homeomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-spec-localization-away-basic-open], the prime of $B$ corresponding to $e$ is contained in $\mathfrak q$. Choose $t\in W_i$ mapping to $e$. Step 4 makes its ambient stalk regular, contrary to its membership in $W_i$. Hence $\mathfrak qB[1/a]$ lies outside every $\overline{E_i}$. The complement of their finite union is an open neighbourhood of that point in $D(a)$.

source.place: Lemma 4.4, closure of each constructible image and exclusion of q, printed p.5; Stacks 094L and 0903(1)

proof.text: View this neighbourhood as an open subset $O\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}B$, using the homeomorphism onto the open $D(a)$ in [lem-weil-pbc-spec-localization-away-basic-open]. Its basic-open-basis clause gives $c\notin\mathfrak q$ with $\mathfrak q\in D(c)\subseteq O$. Set $b=ac$. Then $b\notin\mathfrak q$ and $D(b)\subseteq D(a)$ avoids every $E_i$. Restrict the entire diagram of Step 3 to $D(b)$. The permanence clause of [lem-per-local-alteration-diagram-spreading] gives integral Noetherian $X_i$, an integral Noetherian witness $V$, all the required morphism properties, and the finite indexed open cover with its maps. A nonregular point of $X_i$ above $V(JB[1/b])$ would, as a point of the open $T_{a,i}$, belong to $W_i$ and map into $E_i\cap D(b)$, which is empty. Open restriction leaves stalks unchanged, so every required ambient stalk is regular. These are all the asserted data and properties.

source.place: Lemma 4.4, final principal shrink and computation W_b,i=W_a,i intersect X_b,i, printed p.6; Stacks 00E0 and 00E4
